test.command: cd apps/mobile; bun run typecheck; cd ../..; cd apps/mobile; bun run lint

blockingIssues.description: Hardcoded relative import paths to monorepo packages bypassing the workspace alias (`../../../packages/ui/src/components/ui/button.native`). Should use `@workspace/ui/components/ui/button`. Explicitly including `.native` in the import is also an anti-pattern in React Native / Expo.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Update verification shell commands to be shell-agnostic or PowerShell compatible. Avoid using `&&` and use separate execution lines instead.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: dashboard-screen transcript shows the worker had to manually adapt `&&` to PowerShell syntax `Set-Location ...; ...` because `&&` is invalid.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add boundary: Do not bypass monorepo workspace aliases. Always use `@workspace/ui/components/...` to import shared primitives in the mobile app, and never include explicit `.native` extensions in import paths. Rely on the bundler to resolve platform-specific files.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: auth-screens worker explicitly switched to deeply nested relative imports with `.native` extensions (e.g., `../../../packages/ui/src/components/ui/button.native`) to pass tsc.

rejectedObservations.observation: Worker spent time grepping through packages/calendar-client to discover the calendarApiService methods (getUserSettings, updateUserSettings) and UserSettings types. Documenting core API services and data structures in the library could speed up development.
rejectedObservations.reason: ambiguous; lack of sufficient context to author a comprehensive library file for the calendar-client API without further exploration.
